title: From Navratri to Diwali: Dermatologists' Dos and Don'ts for Festive Skin
excerpt: Nine nights of Garba, late-night parties and weeks of heavy makeup take a toll — dermatologists say the festive glow comes down to preparation, non-comedogenic makeup and double cleansing, not last-minute miracles.
body:
• Dermatologists say the Navratri-to-Diwali stretch is peak season for acne and rashes, driven by heavy makeup, sweat, late nights and pollution.
  • Do: prep skin before makeup, choose non-comedogenic water-based formulas, go light on layers, and double-cleanse — micellar water plus a gentle face wash — every night.
  • Don't: sleep in makeup, over-exfoliate, start strong new actives or retinoids right before events, or overload on sugar and fried food.
  • After Diwali, give skin a gentle reset: mild cleansing, exfoliation once or twice a week, and hydration with hyaluronic acid, glycerin or ceramides.

Nine nights of Garba, a calendar of Diwali parties and weeks of heavy makeup are a recipe for exactly what you don't want on a festival morning: a breakout. As the festive stretch from Navratri to Diwali gets underway, dermatologists say the glow everyone wants is built on unglamorous habits — preparation, the right formulas and relentless cleansing.

Why festivals punish skin

"During the festive season, I often see a surge in acne and rashes. The mix of heavy makeup, sweat, and pollution creates the perfect storm for skin irritation," says Dr. Sheetal Yadav, a board-certified dermatologist.

— Dr. Sheetal Yadav, dermatologist

The problem is rarely makeup itself, but the type — and how it comes off. Many long-wear or oil-based formulas are comedogenic: they clog pores and trap dirt, sweat and bacteria, creating ideal conditions for acne-causing microbes. Certain pigments and preservatives can also trigger allergic or irritant dermatitis — red, itchy patches that no highlighter can fix.

The dos

Dr. Ameesha Mahajan, cosmetic dermatologist and founder of Eden Skin Clinic, advises starting with preparation: cleanse and hydrate thoroughly before makeup, then use a lightweight moisturiser and primer to create a smooth base that keeps residue from clogging pores. Choose non-comedogenic products — water-based foundations and concealers, mineral-based powders — and go light on layers. "Less is more," she notes: heavy foundation mixed with sweat increases the chances of breakouts.

Celebrity cosmetic dermatologist Dr. Chytra V. Anand recommends a pre-festive routine of gentle cleansing, a hyaluronic acid serum for plumpness, a vitamin C serum for brightness and even tone, exfoliation once or twice a week with an enzyme-based product — and, always, broad-spectrum sunscreen.

The single most repeated instruction across every expert: remove makeup thoroughly. Double cleansing — micellar water followed by a gentle face wash — ensures no residue stays behind to clog pores overnight.

The don'ts

Don't sleep in makeup, however late the night runs. Don't over-exfoliate in pursuit of instant brightness; too much strips the barrier and causes irritation instead. Dermatologists also advise pausing potent actives — retinoids and strong exfoliating acids — until skin feels normal again during the heavy-makeup weeks, reintroducing them only after the celebrations.

And don't try aggressive new treatments or facials days before a big event. If you want an in-clinic glow treatment, experts suggest booking it two weeks before the festivities, not two days. Diet matters too: excess sugar drives inflammation that shows up as breakouts, so the festive mithai binge has a visible cost.

The post-Diwali reset

Once the diyas are out, give skin a deliberate recovery. Dr. Nirupama Parwanda, dermatologist and founder of Zolie Skin Clinic, recommends starting with gentle cleansing, then exfoliating once or twice a week with a mild scrub or a chemical exfoliant containing lactic or glycolic acid to clear the dead-cell buildup from weeks of makeup and pollution.

Then, hydration: a moisturising toner or facial mist followed by a lightweight moisturiser with hyaluronic acid, glycerin or ceramides — plus at least eight glasses of water a day to rehydrate from the inside. If skin feels tight or dry, a light sleeping mask or a thicker layer on dry areas helps it hold moisture overnight and recover faster.

Whether you're doing Garba in New Jersey or Diwali in Dallas, the advice travels: the festive glow is built in the weeks before the first diya — not the morning of.
